[Ultraviolet radiation is light from the sun that has shorty, non-visible wave lengths than the visible light spectrum.](http://i.sli.mg/w6h9IK.png) UV light consists of longer wavelenght UVA and sorter UVB. [Both types penetrate the skin](http://i.sli.mg/q3VUIS.png) and lead to premature skin aging, eye damage (including cataracts), and skin cancers. They also suppress the immune system, reducing your ability to fight off these and other maladies. [1]

**UVA** [1]: -95% of UV radiation that reaches Earth's surface. -Present with relatively equal intensity during all daylight hours throughout the year, and can penetrate clouds and glass. -Major part in skin aging and wrinkling (photoaging). -Damages skin cells called keratinocytes in the basal layer of the epidermis, where most skin cancers occur and may initiate the development of skin cancers. -Dominant tanning ray. Tans causes cumulative damage over time. A tan results from injury to the skin's DNA; the skin darkens in an imperfect attempt to prevent further DNA damage. These imperfections, or mutations, can lead to skin cancer. [Side note]:People who use tanning salons are 2.5 times more likely to develop squamous cell carcinoma, and 1.5 times more likely to develop basal cell carcinoma. According to recent research, first exposure to tanning beds in youth increases melanoma risk by 75 percent. If you tan *fucking stop*.

**UVB** [1]: -Chief cause of skin reddening and sunburn. -Damages the skin's more superficial epidermal layers. -Key role in development of skin cancer. -Contributory role in tanning and photoaging. -Intensity varies by season, location, and time of day with UVB rays most intense from 10am-2pm, summar months, an on reflective surfaces like snow.

**Protecting your skin from UV light will help defend you from skin cancer, sun burns, and premature aging.** Sun screen should be worn year round. Physical barriers can also be used such as hats, scarves, body covering clothing, and sunglasses.

Always make sure you use a sunscreen that shields you from *both* UVA and UVB.
